subject: chemistry
title: Relative atomic mass
key_idea: The **relative atomic mass** (Ar) of an element is an average that takes account of the abundance of its isotopes. That is why some relative atomic masses are not whole numbers. Add up each mass number times its percentage and divide by 100.

sections.heading: Why relative atomic mass is an average

blocks.text: A sample of an element usually contains a mixture of isotopes. Ar is an average over all the atoms in the sample.

items.meaning: An average value for the atoms of an element, taking account of the abundance of its isotopes.
The percentage of the atoms in a sample that are a particular isotope.

items: Isotopes have different mass numbers, so the average is rarely a whole number.
Chlorine has two isotopes, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37. Its Ar is 35.5.
The Ar is closer to the mass number of the more abundant isotope.
If two isotopes are equally abundant, the Ar is halfway between their mass numbers.
Ar is an average that takes account of isotope abundance.
Ar is not always a whole number because isotopes have different masses.
The Ar is nearest to the mass number of the most abundant isotope.

blocks.text: Multiply each mass number by its percentage abundance, add the results and divide by 100.

blocks.label: Relative atomic mass
blocks.formula: Ar = [(mass number × percentage of isotope 1) + (mass number × percentage of isotope 2)] ÷ 100
where: Add a term for each extra isotope.
The percentages must add up to 100.

items.text: Chlorine-35 is 75% of the atoms. Chlorine-37 is 25%.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating a relative atomic mass from two isotopes and their percentage abundances.
diagram.question: A sample of an element has two isotopes. **{P}%** of the atoms have mass number 35 and the rest have mass number 37. Calculate the relative atomic mass (Ar) to 1 decimal place.
working: The atoms with mass number 37 make up the rest: (100 − {P})%

items: Multiply each mass number by its percentage, add them up, then divide by 100.
Use all the isotopes in the data, even one with a tiny abundance.
Give the answer to the number of decimal places asked for.

blocks.text: Relative atomic masses are used to find the relative formula mass of a compound. A later topic covers this in full.

items.meaning: The sum of the relative atomic masses (Ar) of all the atoms in the formula. For a molecule it is called relative molecular mass.

blocks.label: Relative formula mass
blocks.formula: Mr = sum of the Ar of all the atoms in the formula
where: Multiply the Ar by the number of atoms of that element.
A number after a bracket multiplies everything inside it.

items.text: Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, has 1 Ca, 2 O and 2 H.

items: Mr is the sum of the Ar values of all the atoms in the formula.
Count the atoms carefully, including those inside brackets.

checks.q: Explain why the relative atomic mass of an element is often not a whole number.
checks.a: The element has isotopes with different mass numbers. The relative atomic mass is an average that takes account of their abundances.

checks.q: An element has two isotopes: mass number 10 (20% of atoms) and mass number 11 (80%). Calculate its relative atomic mass.
Calculate the relative formula mass of MgCl₂ (Ar: Mg = 24, Cl = 35.5).

worked_example.question:
Table 1 shows information about the three isotopes of neon.

Mass number 20: percentage abundance 90.48%
Mass number 21: percentage abundance 0.27%
Mass number 22: percentage abundance 9.25%

Calculate the relative atomic mass (Ar) of neon.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: Marks are for the correct set-up, the unrounded answer and the correct rounding. A correctly rounded answer from an incorrect calculation using all the values also scores the last mark.

worked_example.question:
Lithium has two naturally occurring isotopes, lithium-6 and lithium-7.
A sample of lithium contains
7.59% of lithium-6
92.41% of lithium-7.

Calculate the relative atomic mass of lithium in this sample.
Give your answer to two decimal places.
You must show your working.
worked_example.tip: The correct answer of 6.92 scores 4 marks with or without working. If it is wrong, each step of working can still score.

Calculate the relative formula mass of a (C₂H₅)₂O molecule.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0   H = 1.0   O = 16.0
